one_liner: Notion offers a REST API with personal access tokens and OAuth for integrations.
gating_notes: Personal Access Tokens are self-serve for most users, but on Business and Enterprise plans, PAT creation is restricted by default and requires a workspace owner to enable it in Settings.
oauth_details: OAuth flow is available for connections; internal connections use static API tokens sent as Bearer tokens.

auth_methods.quote: A personal access token (PAT) lets you authenticate API requests as yourself without setting up a connection or completing an OAuth flow.

credential_access.quote: A personal access token (PAT) lets you authenticate API requests as yourself without setting up a connection or completing an OAuth flow. Open [Personal access tokens](https://www.notion.so/developers/tokens) in the Developer portal. Copy the token and save it somewhere secure.

api_type.quote: The API token will be used to authenticate REST API requests.

api_breadth.quote: For requests to pages, databases, and other workspace resources, send an Authorization: Bearer header with your token

Notion provides a free personal access token (PAT) that developers can generate in the Developer portal without any paid plan or sales involvement. This token allows full API access for development and testing.
Notion publishes an official hosted MCP server (notion-mcp-server) as part of its developer platform, making it an official MCP solution.
